notes.text: Overall, the codebase is mature and well-tested. The main concerns are the oversized `response.js` and `test/res.sendFile.js` files, which could benefit from modularization. The deprecated `res.sendfile` has a minor inconsistency with path encoding. The router's param deprecation lacks a removal timeline. The trust proxy back-compat uses a fragile string marker. No critical security issues were found in the provided excerpts. The test files are large but typical for a framework's test suite. The static analysis findings about file sizes are accurate. The duplication in `response.js` (lines 379-398) was not manually verified but is plausible given the file size.

findings.title: Deprecated res.sendfile does not encode path while res.sendFile does
findings.description:
The deprecated `res.sendfile` passes `path` directly to `send` without `encodeURI`, whereas `res.sendFile` uses `encodeURI(path)`. This inconsistency could cause issues with special characters in file paths when using the deprecated method.

> Validation: cited 379-398 does not contain the snippet — actual lines are 501-528; citation corrected
findings.suggestion: Apply `encodeURI` to `path` in `res.sendfile` for consistency, or remove the deprecated method entirely.
findings.benefit: Prevents potential bugs with special characters in file paths for legacy code using `res.sendfile`.
findings.risk: Low; the method is deprecated and users are encouraged to use `res.sendFile`.
